creatures.name: Polyphemus
creatures.poseidonRelation: Son of Poseidon and the nymph Thoosa
creatures.summary: A one-eyed Cyclops blinded by Odysseus.
keyMyths: Odysseus and his men were trapped in his cave (Odyssey, book 9).
Odysseus blinded him with a heated olive stake.
Odysseus told him his name was 'Nobody'.
Polyphemus prayed to Poseidon to make Odysseus's journey long and painful.

facts: Polyphemus is a Cyclops, the son of Poseidon and the nymph Thoosa.
In the Odyssey he traps Odysseus and his men in his cave and eats several of them.
Odysseus blinds him with a sharpened stake and calls himself 'Nobody'.
Polyphemus prays to Poseidon to prevent Odysseus reaching home.

lines: My son. A brute, but mine. Do not speak of his blinding lightly, you mortal.
He prayed and I answered. Odysseus learned what it costs to mock my blood.
Nobody? A clever trick indeed. Cleverness is not the same thing as safety on my sea.

creatures.name: Pegasus
creatures.poseidonRelation: Son of Poseidon and the Gorgon Medusa
creatures.summary: A winged horse born from Medusa when Perseus beheaded her.
keyMyths: Pegasus and his brother Chrysaor sprang from Medusa when Perseus cut off her head.
He is said to be named after the springs (pegai) near where he was born.
Bellerophon tamed him with a golden bridle from Athena.
Bellerophon and Pegasus killed the Chimera.
When Bellerophon tried to fly to Olympus, Pegasus threw him off.
Pegasus then served Zeus and carried his thunderbolts.
His hoof striking Mount Helicon created the Hippocrene spring, sacred to the Muses.

facts: In Hesiod's Theogony, Pegasus is the offspring of Poseidon and Medusa.
He and Chrysaor emerged when Perseus beheaded Medusa.
Athena's golden bridle let Bellerophon tame him (Pindar).
Sources differ on details, such as how Poseidon and Medusa came together.

lines: Born of my blood and the Gorgon's. Even I could not hold him to the earth.
A horse of the sea made flesh, and he chose the sky. I forgive him.
Do not ask me about the Gorgon. Ask about the horse.
